clue.text: Entertainment featuring nude in naughty act

indicators.note: in places the nude word inside the scrambled act
naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so the word act is scrambled

parts.note: nude means bare

explanation.surface: A risqué show includes a naked turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges ACT into CAT, and 'in' puts BARE inside it: CA(BARE)T. 'featuring' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a kind of nightclub show, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Material, a metal, found in small mechanical component

indicators.note: found in puts the article and metal inside the component

parts.note: a cog is a small toothed part of a machine
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A metal part turns up in a small machine component.
explanation.walkthrough: A and TIN go inside COG: CO(ATIN)G.
explanation.definitionFit: A coating is a layer of material covering a surface.

clue.text: Sea around Long Island associated with movement of missiles

indicators.note: around means the sea surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe

explanation.surface: Missiles cross the waters off Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long Island' is not LI here but L and IS, which go inside BALTIC: BAL(LIS)TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistics is the science of projectiles in flight, so ballistic relates to missiles' motion.

clue.text: Crest fellow removed from domestic appliance

indicators.note: removed from says the fellow's letter is taken out of the appliance

parts.note: a fridge is a kitchen appliance

explanation.surface: A man is ejected from a kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the narrow top of a hill, its crest.

clue.text: Ready to spill the beans in lecture on rise of Peron

parts.note: a talk is a lecture

indicators.note: rise of in a down clue means the name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Evita was Eva Peron, wife of the Argentine president

explanation.surface: A lecture on Eva Peron's rise to power makes someone chatty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' reverses EVITA to ATIVE, which goes after TALK. 'in' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty person is ready to talk, quick to reveal secrets.

clue.text: Casually fires on vessel after repelling boarders here

indicators.note: repelling means pushing back, so the pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to pot or take pot shots is to fire casually
a sub (submarine) is a vessel

explanation.surface: Sailors take pot shots from a ship after beating off pirates trying to board.
explanation.walkthrough: POTS on SUB gives POTSSUB, and 'after repelling' turns the whole run backwards. 'Boarders' sounds piratical, but they are passengers getting on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers board buses at a stop, so it is where boarders get on.

clue.text: Seating for washer?

parts.note: a washer sounds like a ring in plumbing, but here it is a person washing, who sits on this

explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin a person sits on to wash.

clue.text: Coat is associated with Cotswold family

parts.note: the Cotswold is an English breed of sheep
is shortened to 's
kin means family

explanation.surface: A coat goes with a family from the Cotswolds, the English hill region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotswold' suggests the hills in southern England; it is a breed of sheep. 'is' gives 'S, as in it's.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a coat made from a sheep's pelt with the fleece left on.

clue.text: Invite office worker out at last

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word out

explanation.surface: Ask a temporary secretary out at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to entice or lure, as an invitation may.

clue.text: Articles eaten by priest's cat

indicators.note: eaten by puts the articles inside the priest's abbreviation

parts.note: PR is short for priest
an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A priest's cat devours some objects.
explanation.walkthrough: AN and THE go inside PR: P(ANTHE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard.

clue.text: Withdrawn girl is troubled

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Delia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy girl is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To be troubled by illness is to have been unwell, suffering.

clue.text: Seducer put out denials, having kept mum

indicators.note: having kept means holding something inside
put out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: mum is mother, MA

explanation.surface: A womaniser issues denials while his mother keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges DENIALS into LADIESN, and 'having kept' holds MA inside: LADIES(MA)N. 'mum' looks like 'silent' but is mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a charmer who woos women, a seducer.

clue.text: Travelling Italian taking time, long time, in pub

indicators.note: taking means the outer pieces take in what follows
in places the long period inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An Italian spends ages in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: ERA goes 'in' INN to make INERAN, and IT plus T 'taking' that gives IT(INERAN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant person moves from place to place, travelling as a way of life.

clue.text: Where you'll see players in cast

definitions.meaning: a sports field where the teams play
to throw, as in ... a ball

explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is a football or cricket field, and to pitch is to throw or toss.

clue.text: Dress surface

definitions.meaning: an outfit, especially an unusual one
as a verb, to rise or come up, as from bed

explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is a costume, and to get up is to rise, as a diver does on surfacing.

clue.text: Make a mark, periodically

parts.note: seems to mean leaving a mark now and then, but a period is a full stop

explanation.definitionFit: To punctuate is to put in full stops and commas, and also to interrupt at intervals.

clue.text: Performer always on edge

parts.note: a nervous performer on the surface, but literally one balanced on a blade's edge on the rink

explanation.definitionFit: A figure skater performs on the narrow edges of skate blades.

clue.text: Reflect on changes in one of the characters on the staff

definitions.text: one of the characters on the staff

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Think about changes among the people working somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor clef is a sign placed on the musical stave to fix pitch.

clue.text: Yarn producer

parts.note: looks like a spinner of wool, but a yarn is also a tale

explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, one who spins tales.

clue.text: Figure given brush off to receive merit award

indicators.note: to receive means holding the award inside
off suggests the letters of the word brush are disrupted

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone snubbed is about to be honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges BRUSH into RHBUS, and 'to receive' puts OM inside: RH(OM)BUS. 'brush off' looks like a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure, a parallelogram with equal sides.

clue.text: Individual seen in Nova Scotia church service

indicators.note: seen in places the individual inside the province's abbreviation

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for Nova Scotia, a Canadian province
a single individual is one

explanation.surface: A lone person attends a church service in Nova Scotia.
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is one of the canonical hours, a short daily office said in the afternoon.

clue.text: Hide in trees growing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hide in trees growing (7)': an anagram of 'trees' lacks the C and E of the answer, so a word appears to be missing; no scan or source found.

clue.text: Bird caged by returning hotel worker

indicators.note: returning says the enclosed letters are read backwards
caged by says the letters sit enclosed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird is kept in a cage by a hotel employee.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Bird caged' as definition, leaving no hidden indicator; 'caged by' signals the run TELWO across 'hotel worker', and 'returning' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Poem richly ornamented, not Heine's first

indicators.note: ornamented suggests the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement
first picks the opening letter of Heine's

explanation.surface: A poem richly decorated, not one by Heine.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RICHLY are rearranged to give the answer plus H, the first letter of 'Heine's'; 'not' tells you that H is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing feeling, often set to music.

clue.text: See pibroch is to be played

indicators.note: to be played suggests the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A Highland bagpipe tune is about to be performed.
explanation.walkthrough: A pibroch is a set of variations for the Scottish bagpipes. 'See' is a bishop's diocese, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area under a bishop's authority, its diocese.

clue.text: It's sure to be seen in spring

definitions.meaning: certain, as in '... to be seen'

explanation.surface: Something is certain to be seen in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound to means certain to, and a bound is a leap or spring.

clue.text: Promotion involving copper in Scottish island, a terrific swimmer?

indicators.note: in places the promotion with copper inside the island's name

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides

indicators.note: involving means taking the metal's symbol into the advert

parts.note: an ad is a promotion
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Publicity for a policeman on a Hebridean island, along with a great swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: CU goes into AD for ACUD, which goes 'in' BARRA before its last A: BARR(ACUD)A. 'copper' looks like a policeman. The question mark marks 'terrific' as terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A barracuda is a large predatory fish, a frightening swimmer.

clue.text: Find answers to clues? Only about five

indicators.note: about means surrounding the Roman numeral

parts.note: sole means only
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A solver has only about five answers.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve clues is to work out what they mean, the crossword's whole point.

clue.text: Come after work

definitions.meaning: to follow in sequence, as an heir does

explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to follow someone in office, and also to be successful, as a plan that works.

clue.text: Grab a bit

explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is to seize something, and a snaffle is a simple jointed bit for a horse.
